pages.text: "Bread!" Impatient Bobo ran to the long table by the window. Teacher Bau was setting down a plate. Bobo grabbed bread with hands covered in potting soil.
"Bobo, what about your hands?" asked Mio, who did everything alone. "It takes too long to go and wash! I am eating now!" Bobo pulled the hat brim forward and munched.
Black handprints dotted the bread. Beside it, Mio's bread was white and fluffy. Bobo finished and dashed into the yard.
But rumble, rumble went the tummy. A little ache began. "Oh, my tummy..." Bobo hugged their belly and sat down.
Bobo lay on the classroom mat. Friends' laughter came through the window. More than anything, Bobo wanted to play, but could not today.
After a while, the tummy felt a little better. Mio held Bobo's hand and led the way to wash. They stood together before the mirror.
Mio called, "One, wet with water!" Water poured. "Two, bubbly soap!" White foam covered Bobo's hands. "Three, squeaky clean between the fingers! Hands washed first, bread after!"
Teacher Bau studied Bobo's hands. "Tiny things you cannot see cling to soil. They travel from hands to bread." Bobo leaned forward to examine both palms.
The next day, when bread arrived, Bobo called first, "Wait! Hands first!" One, wet; two, bubbles; three, clean—Bobo did it all alone.
Teacher Bau patted Bobo's back. Washing before picking up bread meant no tummyache and no marks on the bread. Holding bread in clean hands, Bobo said, "Hands washed first, bread after!"
